- **Separate waves.** Fit one cross-sectional model per wave, with one row per child. A stacked random-intercept model would change the estimand. The wave with the most observed outcomes supplies the standard diagnostic trace and plots; ties use the latest wave. This is an operational choice, not a primary outcome or power claim. Tables report convergence for every mutually adjusted fit and single-skill, trait-adjusted comparator.
- **Skill predictors.** Use standardised same-wave logits with regularising `Normal(0, 0.3)` slopes for the small, collinear sample. Exclude floored measures (`P`, `N`) as predictors.
- **Trait covariates.** Use t1 non-verbal ability, hearing, speech and phonological memory at every wave (#371).
- **Group.** Include arm as a nuisance term for wave-specific composition; do not report it as an association.
- **Missingness.** Mean-impute missing skill predictors to zero on their standardised scale and report observed/imputed counts. Conditional coefficients can be biased in either direction. Hearing, speech and phonological memory have missingness indicators; omit indicators constant among that wave's observed-outcome rows and treat the others as nuisance offsets. Drop rows missing the focal outcome.
